section_summary: The section closes statistical appendices on Japanese textile manufacturers, rayon capacity, silk filatures, wool production, and trade associations, then reproduces wartime textile control regulations. Correspondence and telegrams from December 1945 through February 1946 concern the proposed textile mission to Japan, its membership and travel through Korea, and plans to supply American cotton for Japanese textile production. Several telegrams and arrival notices appear in duplicate copies.

subfiles.title: Appendix II, textile manufacturers and addresses
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese textile manufacturers' associations and their addresses.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages continue a geographic directory of rayon, silk, cotton and other weaving associations.

subfiles.title: Appendix II-3: Estimated capacity of Japanese rayon pulp mills
subfiles.about: Tabulates rayon pulp mills in Japan and capacity lost after surrender.
subfiles.summary: Estimates mill capacity by location and company.

subfiles.title: Appendix II-4: Annual capacities of thirty principal rayon and staple fibre mills
subfiles.about: Ranks major rayon and staple fibre mills by estimated annual capacity.
subfiles.summary: The table identifies mills, owners and prefectures, and estimates aggregate rayon and staple fibre capacity. Notes explain approximate rankings and ranges.

subfiles.title: Appendix III-1: Two leading firms in the silk industry
subfiles.about: Profiles Katakura and Gunze silk companies.
subfiles.summary: Provides subsidiaries, offices, capitalization, directors, facilities and output for two leading silk firms.

subfiles.title: Appendix III-2: Silk industry federations
subfiles.about: Lists national silk industry federations.
subfiles.summary: Names federations for silk raisers, egg producers, reelers, exporters and merchants.

subfiles.title: Appendix III-3: Chief raw silk filatures
subfiles.about: Lists major raw silk filatures, reeling basins and output.
subfiles.summary: A prefecture-by-prefecture table identifies large filatures and compares their fitted reeling basins and annual export raw silk output. Its source is The Japan Silk Yearbook, 1935–1936.

subfiles.title: Appendix IV-1: Japan Woolen Industry Association
subfiles.about: Lists wool industry association firms and addresses.
subfiles.summary: A directory of member firms, offices and locations.

subfiles.title: Appendix IV-2: Concentration of woolen production
subfiles.about: Compares spinning and loom capacity among ten major wool firms.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates spindles and looms, showing the leading firms' share of association capacity.

subfiles.title: Appendix V: National federations in the Japanese textiles industry
subfiles.about: Lists manufacturers', merchants' and exporters' federations.
subfiles.summary: The appendix names textile federations in English and romanized Japanese, covering fibres, finished goods and export markets.

subfiles.title: Note on omitted Control Society exhibits
subfiles.about: Explains why four textile control society exhibits are absent from some copies.
subfiles.summary: Limited copies of a source report prevented inclusion of Exhibits VI-1 through VI-4.

subfiles.title: Regulations of the Woolen Goods Control Society
subfiles.about: Sets out the Woolen Goods Control Society's powers, membership and governance.
subfiles.summary: The regulations cover production and distribution controls, prices, officers, conferences, accounting, dissolution and penalties. They place the society under the Minister of Commerce and empower its president to direct wool industry affairs.

subfiles.title: Appendix VI-6: Control Regulations of the Fabric Control Society
subfiles.about: Defines the Fabric Control Society's authority over textile production and business operations.
subfiles.summary: Twenty-six provisions govern products, resources, labour, equipment, business plans, contracts, accounts and reporting. Measures involving military supplies require Army and Navy approval.

subfiles.title: Rose accepts appointment to textile mission
subfiles.about: Accepts the textile mission appointment and awaits travel instructions.
subfiles.summary: Rose is collecting material to aid the mission.

subfiles.title: Recommendation of Peter Frederick Nagagna as silk expert
subfiles.about: Recommends Nagagna for possible service as a silk expert in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Borton forwards his qualifications and asks to be informed of the decision.

subfiles.title: Request for news release on Comer mission
subfiles.about: Requests publishable information on Hugh Comer's planned Japan trip.
subfiles.summary: Dalton offers to forward a release to Southern newspapers.

subfiles.title: Reply to Dalton on forthcoming mission release
subfiles.about: Promises a State Department release when participating countries announce the mission.
subfiles.summary: Martin expects a coordinated international release shortly.

subfiles.title: Appointment and objectives for textile mission executive secretary
subfiles.about: Confirms Taylor's mission role and describes the textile survey's policy objectives.
subfiles.summary: Thorp asks for an appraisal of Japanese capacity in 1946–1947, especially cotton textiles available for export after domestic needs. The mission should examine raw material and repair requirements and produce a policy report. Taylor may subsequently survey Chinese textiles.

subfiles.title: Comer acknowledges mission invitation
subfiles.about: Thanks Thorp for inviting him on the textile mission.
subfiles.summary: Comer awaits departure and promises a useful report.

subfiles.title: Rose on rayon supplies and mission arrangements
subfiles.about: Raises concerns about sulphuric acid availability and requests support for the survey.
subfiles.summary: Rose says removal of Japan's sulphuric acid industry could disable viscose rayon production. He is collecting plant information and asks for interpreters and Army officers to support field groups.

subfiles.title: Martin replies on sulphuric acid and survey facilities
subfiles.about: Addresses sulphuric acid reparations discussions and mission travel support.
subfiles.summary: Martin says rayon requirements will be considered and expects necessary survey facilities after agreement with the Supreme Commander.

subfiles.title: Becker accepts Bunce mission terms
subfiles.about: Accepts a Bunce mission position subject to salary and transfer arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Becker seeks guidance on transfer from the Forest Service with reemployment rights.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Becker acceptance telegram
subfiles.about: Duplicates Becker's acceptance and transfer questions.
subfiles.summary: A second filed copy of the preceding telegram.

subfiles.title: Comer requests withdrawal from textile mission
subfiles.about: Explains why delayed departure and a longer trip require him to withdraw.
subfiles.summary: Comer cites February commitments, Avondale business and a proposed China venture. He doubts his survey contribution is essential but offers to reconsider if the government needs him.

subfiles.title: Thorp acknowledges Comer's withdrawal
subfiles.about: Thanks Comer for preparing to serve and expresses regret at his withdrawal.
subfiles.summary: Thorp hopes officials can discuss the mission report with Comer.

subfiles.title: Textile exporters request consultation
subfiles.about: Asks that American textile producers and exporters be heard before decisions on Japan.
subfiles.summary: The association thanks Thorp and awaits the mission report.

subfiles.title: Appointment date wired to Becker
subfiles.about: Sets Becker's Bunce mission appointment effective January 1.
subfiles.summary: A formal appointment letter will follow.

subfiles.title: Donald Comer declines trip and suggests Calloway
subfiles.about: Confirms both Comer brothers are unavailable and recommends Cason Calloway.
subfiles.summary: He cites Calloway's participation in a 1937 Japanese textile mission.

subfiles.title: Chinese Embassy names mission observer
subfiles.about: Designates Yang Sih-Zung as China's textile mission representative.
subfiles.summary: Yang will travel directly from China to Japan.

subfiles.title: Comer explains withdrawal in greater detail
subfiles.about: Explains schedule and labour concerns behind his withdrawal.
subfiles.summary: Comer and his brother remain willing to discuss textile questions.

subfiles.title: Mission composition and Chinese delegate arrangements
subfiles.about: Lists international mission members and requests help for the Chinese delegate.
subfiles.summary: The embassy may assist Yang and his secretary in meeting the group in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Travel instructions to Appenzeller
subfiles.about: Provides the Bunce group's expected flight and Hawaii joining arrangements.
subfiles.summary: Appenzeller will receive arrival details from Hamilton Field.

subfiles.title: Travel instructions to Becker
subfiles.about: Directs Becker to Hamilton Field for processing and the February 2 flight.
subfiles.summary: Becker is told to retain travel receipts.

subfiles.title: Travel instructions to Braden
subfiles.about: Directs Braden to Hamilton Field for the Bunce group flight.
subfiles.summary: Braden is told to retain travel receipts.

subfiles.title: Request for Bunce group quarters in Seoul
subfiles.about: Requests temporary and permanent accommodation for the Bunce group.
subfiles.summary: The group seeks billeting, meals and habitable mission houses.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: Designates a white telegram copy as the record copy.
subfiles.summary: The yellow action copy was not returned.

subfiles.title: Benninghoff asks about Bunce group pay and stenographer
subfiles.about: Requests pay authorization documents and confirmation of Miss Hays's assignment.
subfiles.summary: He needs a stenographer if Hays is unavailable to his office.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Benninghoff's February 7 telegram
subfiles.about: Duplicates the request about pay documents and Miss Hays.
subfiles.summary: A second filed copy of the preceding telegram.

subfiles.title: Bunce group arrival report
subfiles.about: Reports the group's February 11 arrival in Seoul.
subfiles.summary: Benninghoff asks that named family members be notified.

subfiles.title: U.S. Commercial Company accepts cotton arrangement
subfiles.about: Accepts an agreement for U.S. cotton to be manufactured into textiles in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Henderson forwards the Agriculture Secretary's letter with company acceptance noted.
